title: Heart-failure pleural effusion is transudative: low protein and low lactate dehydrogenase
vignette: Item 2 of 2. On physical examination, jugular venous pressure is elevated, breath sounds are decreased at the right lung base with dullness to percussion, and 2+ bilateral lower extremity pitting edema is present. Chest x-ray shows cephalization of the blood vessels, Kerley B lines, and a right pleural effusion. Thoracentesis is performed for pleural fluid analysis. In comparison to plasma fluid, which of the following pleural fluid findings is most likely to be observed?

clues.note: Elevated JVP indicates systemic venous congestion from heart failure - a cause of TRANSUDATIVE pleural effusion.

clues.text: 2+ bilateral lower extremity pitting edema is present
clues.note: Bilateral pitting edema plus elevated JVP confirms heart failure with fluid overload.

clues.text: cephalization of the blood vessels, Kerley B lines, and a right pleural effusion
clues.note: Cephalization and Kerley B lines are radiographic signs of elevated pulmonary venous pressure (heart failure), which produces a TRANSUDATIVE effusion.

whatMatters: Heart failure raises hydrostatic pressure, causing a TRANSUDATIVE pleural effusion. Transudates have LOW protein and LOW LACTATE DEHYDROGENASE (LDH) relative to plasma (they fail Light criteria). Answer E (low LDH content).
strategy: Classify the effusion by mechanism: heart failure = increased HYDROSTATIC pressure = TRANSUDATE (low protein, low LDH). Use Light criteria - transudates are BELOW the exudative cutoffs. Reject exudate/other-source features: high protein and high WBC (exudates from inflammation/infection/malignancy), low glucose (infectious/malignant/rheumatoid exudate consuming glucose), and high amylase (pancreatitis/esophageal rupture) - none fit a cardiogenic transudate.

eliminations.label: High amylase - pancreatitis/esophageal rupture
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: elevated pleural amylase (pancreatitis, pancreatic pseudocyst, esophageal rupture). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: those cause EXUDATIVE effusions, not the cardiogenic transudate here. ✅ Correct if: pancreatic/esophageal source.

eliminations.label: High protein - exudate
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: high pleural protein (pleural/serum protein >0.5) defining an EXUDATE. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: transudates from heart failure have LOW protein (increased hydrostatic pressure, not increased capillary permeability). ✅ Correct if: exudate from infection/malignancy/inflammation.

eliminations.label: High white blood cell count - exudate (infection/malignancy)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a high leukocyte count (complicated parapneumonic/malignant effusion). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: transudates do NOT show high WBC counts; heart failure effusions are paucicellular. ✅ Correct if: infected/inflammatory exudate.

eliminations.label: Low glucose - infectious/malignant/rheumatoid exudate
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: low pleural glucose from consumption by bacteria/neutrophils/malignant cells. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: that indicates an EXUDATE (empyema, malignancy, rheumatoid), not a cardiogenic transudate. ✅ Correct if: empyema/rheumatoid/malignant effusion with low glucose.

reasoning: Elevated JVP, pitting edema, cephalization, and Kerley B lines indicate heart failure
Heart failure increases pulmonary capillary HYDROSTATIC pressure -> transudative effusion
Transudates have LOW protein and LOW lactate dehydrogenase relative to plasma
-> low lactate dehydrogenase content; answer E
mechanism: Pleural effusions are classified as TRANSUDATIVE or EXUDATIVE, a distinction guided by LIGHT'S CRITERIA (an effusion is EXUDATIVE if any is met: pleural/serum PROTEIN >0.5, pleural/serum LDH >0.6, or pleural LDH > two-thirds the upper limit of normal serum LDH). TRANSUDATIVE effusions form from an imbalance in HYDROSTATIC or ONCOTIC pressure with INTACT capillaries, so relatively little protein and LDH leak into the pleural space - i.e., LOW pleural PROTEIN and LOW LDH compared with plasma. HEART FAILURE causes a transudate: backup of blood from the failing left ventricle raises pulmonary capillary HYDROSTATIC pressure, driving low-protein fluid into the pleural space (cephalization and Kerley B lines reflect this elevated pulmonary venous pressure; elevated JVP and pedal edema reflect systemic congestion). Other transudate causes include cirrhosis (hepatic hydrothorax) and nephrotic syndrome (low oncotic pressure). By contrast, EXUDATES arise from increased capillary PERMEABILITY (infection, malignancy, rheumatologic disease) and show HIGH protein/LDH (and sometimes high WBC, low glucose, or high amylase). Therefore this cardiogenic effusion shows LOW LDH.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Pulm > pleural effusions: Light criteria (protein >0.5, LDH >0.6, or LDH > 2/3 ULN = exudate); transudate = low protein/LDH (heart failure, cirrhosis, nephrotic); exudate = high protein/LDH (infection, malignancy, rheumatologic; +/- low glucose, high amylase, high WBC).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Heart failure = hydrostatic transudate = low protein and low LDH.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on transudate vs exudate, Light criteria, LDH/protein, hydrostatic vs oncotic pressure, or Kerley B lines? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: High protein/WBC, low glucose, high amylase = EXUDATE features (infection/malignancy/pancreatic), not a cardiogenic transudate.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: heart-failure effusion = transudate (low protein, low LDH); exudate = high protein/LDH (Light criteria).

keywords.back: Pleural/serum protein >0.5, LDH >0.6, or LDH > 2/3 ULN serum
Heart failure, cirrhosis (hepatic hydrothorax), nephrotic syndrome

firstAid.detail: Pulm: heart failure -> low protein, low LDH.
Pulm > high protein/LDH/WBC, low glucose, high amylase.

memoryHook: A failing heart just squeezes low-protein water into the chest (pressure, not inflammation) - a transudate: low protein AND low LDH.
